/-!
# Erdős Problem 1214

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1214](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1214)
- [CoSc97] Corrales-Rodrigáñez, Capi and Schoof, René, The support problem and its
  elliptic analogue. J. Number Theory (1997) [Volume 64, Issue 2], 276--290.
-/

namespace Erdos1214

/--
Let $x,y\geq 1$ be integers such that, for all $n\geq 1$, the set of primes dividing $x^{n}-1$ is
equal to the set of primes dividing $y^n-1$. Must $x=y$?

Erdős asked this at a 1988 number theory conference in Banff.

A positive answer was given by Corrales-Rodrigáñez and Schoof [CoSc97].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1214 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ x y : ℕ, x ≥ 1 → y ≥ 1 →
      (∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 1 → { p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ∣ x ^ n - 1 } = { p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ∣ y ^ n - 1 }) →
      x = y := by
  sorry

end Erdos1214

reformulations.difference: Lean uses positive natural numbers and natural-number subtraction where the source speaks of positive integers and ordinary subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For x ≥ 1, one has x^n ≥ 1, so casting the natural-number difference x^n − 1 to ℤ gives exactly (x : ℤ)^n − 1. Divisibility is preserved and reflected by this cast, hence the prime-divisor sets agree. Positive integers correspond bijectively to natural numbers ≥ 1. The equivalence of the complete quantified claims was proved as Review1214.natClaim_iff_intClaim in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Corrales-Rodrigáñez and Schoof, The support problem and its elliptic analogue, Journal of Number Theory 64 (1997), 276–290, especially the Question in §1 and Theorem 1 with its proof in §2: https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~schoof/supp.pdf
Erratum to the cited paper (correction to the diagram on page 283): https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~schoof/errordiag.pdf
Schoof’s publications page, linking the paper and erratum: https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~schoof/papers.html
review.notes: The cited paper states exactly this question and explicitly answers it affirmatively, supporting both answer(True) and research solved. The erratum concerns only a diagram in the elliptic section. Lean checks verified the quantifier scope, prime-divisor-set semantics, satisfiable hypotheses, and boundary cases: x = 1 gives all primes, and 2^1 − 1 gives the empty prime-divisor set. All final scratch checks compiled without errors or warnings. The live erdosproblems.com page returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive user agents; the mathematical statement and solution status were checked against the cited primary paper instead. The reviewed file was not modified.
